name: Harcourt Trophies Grade 2 Teacher Edition — Full Curriculum Architecture
sourceFilesNote: This curriculum analysis and ref-2026-07-18-harcourt-trophies-2nd-lesson-planner share Slack drop 1784407931.510559 and the same four source images. The durable originals stay canonical under the reference record, with no duplicate Blob upload.

principles: Story-as-hub: one reading selection per week powers every skill strand
Spiral review: introduce → practice → generalize → apply → assess within one week
Integrated language arts: phonics, spelling, vocabulary, grammar, writing all taught through/alongside the reading selection
Cross-curricular extension: the week's story theme drives science, social studies, drama, and technology centers
Leveled differentiation: every day has below-level, on-level, advanced, and ELL variants available
layer1_philosophy.learningTheory: spiral with mastery checkpoints (weekly post-test on spelling, end-of-selection assessment on comprehension)
layer1_philosophy.assessmentApproach: structured three-part assessment per story (vocabulary MC → comprehension MC → written response)
layer1_philosophy.parentRole: teacher-facilitator (teacher guide provides full scripted lessons with IF/THEN branching for struggling readers)

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Balanced Literacy (Harcourt Trophies)
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: Story-centered weekly units where a single reading selection drives all ELA skill strands plus cross-curricular centers. Combines explicit phonics instruction with literature-based comprehension and integrated writing.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Story-as-Hub Weekly Format
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: One reading selection per week. All phonics, spelling, vocabulary, grammar, writing, and cross-curricular activities connect to the story. 5-day arc: introduce → practice → generalize → apply → assess. Teacher guide provides day-by-day scripted lessons.

layer3_structure.weeklyTemplate: Every day: Oral Language (15m) + Word Work: phonics+spelling+vocab (35m) + Read (30m) + Language Arts: writing+grammar (30m) + Daily Language Practice (5m) + Independent Reading (15m). Cross-curricular centers rotate through the week (1 per day, 15-30 min each). Total: ~2.5 hours/day.
layer3_structure.progressionModel: spiral within each week (introduce → practice → generalize → apply → assess), with new story + new skills each subsequent week
layer3_structure.reviewRhythm: Daily language practice = spiral review of all previous skills. Weekly spelling post-test. End-of-selection assessment (vocab + comprehension + writing) per story. Mid-year and end-of-year cumulative tests.

dailyArc.day1: Introduce: new story read-aloud, introduce phonics pattern, spelling pretest, introduce grammar concept. Heavy teacher-led modeling.
dailyArc.day2: Practice: read the main selection, build spelling words, introduce vocab, review grammar. Child interacts with the text.
dailyArc.day3: Generalize: reread for fluency, state spelling generalization, connected nonfiction reading. Making patterns explicit.
dailyArc.day4: Apply: comprehension assessment practice, spelling review, writing prompt, grammar review. Testing understanding.
dailyArc.day5: Assess: spelling post-test with writing application, fluency rereading, self-selected reading/writing, grammar test. Celebrating mastery.

notes: This is not just a curriculum ingestion — it's an architecture blueprint. Carolyng's four drops from the same Trophies book (practice pages, assessments, lesson planner, day detail pages) collectively revealed the full four-layer system that makes a published curriculum feel 'complete.' The key product insight: Homa has the Practice Materials layer (materials-studio) and the beginning of curriculum planning (curriculum-studio), but is completely missing the Lesson Planner layer (weekly orchestration), the Daily Instruction layer (how to teach), and the Assessment layer (how to verify). Building the lesson-planner skill closes all three gaps.
